briefs.headline: Cubs rout the Pirates 12-2 as Bregman homers and Dotel falls to 1-5
briefs.summary: Alex Bregman went 3-for-4 with his 25th homer and Michael Busch doubled in three runs Friday at Wrigley Field, where Chicago scored nine in the second through fourth; Bryan Reynolds homered for Pittsburgh. Skenes starts at 2:20 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Brewers shut out the Reds 20-0 as Abbott allows eight runs in two innings
briefs.summary: Garrett Mitchell hit a grand slam and Bryce Turang, William Contreras and Jake Bauers also homered Friday as Milwaukee scored eight in the fifth; Andrew Abbott allowed nine hits and eight runs in two innings. Singer starts at 7:10 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Stewart is doubtful and Turner is a go as the Bengals close their first report
briefs.summary: Zac Taylor said DJ Turner II (hamstring) is 'good to go' Sunday against Tampa Bay; end Shemar Stewart (knee) sat out Friday and is doubtful. Ja'Marr Chase rested Friday and Tee Higgins was full all week; kickoff is 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Browns rule Jenkins out and start rookie Barber at right guard at Jacksonville
briefs.summary: Guard Teven Jenkins (back) is out for Sunday's opener after missing practice Thursday and Friday; rookie Austin Barber starts in his place and center Parker Brailsford (thumb) is questionable. Kickoff at Jacksonville is 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Alonso rates Joao Pedro with Haaland before Hull City visits Stamford Bridge
briefs.summary: Xabi Alonso said Friday that Joao Pedro, August's Premier League player of the month with two goals and two assists in three matches, 'reminds me of Benzema' and is on Erling Haaland's level. Hull visits Saturday at 10 a.m. ET (3 p.m. BST).

briefs.headline: Gakpo is a doubt for Fulham after missing training, Iraola says
briefs.summary: Andoni Iraola said Friday that Cody Gakpo 'didn't train yesterday' and would be tested before Fulham, that Barcola's midweek exit was 'just cramps' and that Hugo Ekitike is 'still far' from returning. Kickoff is 10 a.m. ET (3 p.m. BST).

briefs.headline: De Zerbi has Maddison back for Everton and calls Mudryk's injury 'stupid'
briefs.summary: Roberto De Zerbi said Friday that James Maddison is available, Mohammed Kudus is 'very close to being ready to start' and Kulusevski's absence is 'not big problem'; Mudryk's injury was 'stupid.' Everton visits at 12:30 p.m. ET (5:30 BST).

briefs.headline: WVU chases its first two-win start since 2018 against UT Martin
briefs.summary: West Virginia has not opened with two wins since 2018. UT Martin, which beat Chicago State last week, has been coached by Jason Simpson since 2006; Rich Rodriguez called the Skyhawks 'a really good 1AA FCS program.' Kickoff in Morgantown is 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Payne's eight catches give Del Rio-Wilson a 'staple' as Marshall opens at home
briefs.summary: Tight end Toby Payne caught a career-high eight passes for 55 yards at Penn State; Tony Gibson said 'he played well' but 'we couldn't throw the ball downfield because we couldn't protect.' Middle Tennessee, unbeaten after one game, visits at 7 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Ohio opens at home against Jacksonville State in a Cure Bowl rematch
briefs.summary: Ohio, winless after its loss at Nebraska, hosts Jacksonville State, which split its first two games and lost the 2024 Cure Bowl to the Bobcats, Saturday at 6 p.m. ET at Peden Stadium. 'Ohio doesn't beat Ohio,' John Hauser said.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati is without Evander for Charlotte after two straight losses
briefs.summary: Evander is suspended for yellow-card accumulation when Charlotte, fifth in the East with 39 points, visits TQL Stadium Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on Apple TV. 'We're not replacing him. We're trying to adjust without him,' Pat Noonan said.

briefs.headline: Aki basho opens tomorrow with Onosato the lone yokozuna
briefs.summary: The JSA blessed the ring at Ryogoku Kokugikan on Saturday, one day before the Aki basho (autumn tournament) opens without yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu; July champion Aonishiki said he will 'aim for the yusho (championship).'

briefs.headline: Judging chief wants results and 'content' from Kirishima's run
briefs.summary: Ozeki (champion) Kirishima, 30, who won 12 of 15 in July, starts a second straight tsunatori (yokozuna promotion bid) Sunday against Kotoshoho; judging chief Asakayama said 'it is not just about winning' and sumo content must match the results.

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu lost nearly 10 kg before withdrawing, stablemaster says
briefs.summary: Stablemaster Tatsunami said Hoshoryu, 27, lost his appetite, slept poorly and dropped nearly 10 kilograms after July 29 knee surgery before his kyujo (withdrawal), his fifth in 10 basho as yokozuna; Wakatakakage and Wakanosho are also out.

briefs.headline: Rays clinch first on Caminero's walk-off homer, 3-1 over Houston
briefs.summary: Junior Caminero's 40th homer in the ninth Friday at Tropicana Field made Tampa Bay the first team into the 2026 playoffs after two years out; the Rays, 88-59, lead the Yankees by three in the AL East with 15 to play.

briefs.headline: Brewers clinch a playoff berth with a 20-0 rout of Cincinnati
briefs.summary: Garrett Mitchell's grand slam led a 23-hit night Friday in Milwaukee, the largest clinch-day margin on record, and the Brewers, 92-56, are in the postseason for the eighth time in nine seasons.

briefs.headline: Dodgers put Ohtani on the 15-day injured list with biceps trouble
briefs.summary: Los Angeles placed Shohei Ohtani on the 15-day IL Friday with right biceps inflammation, backdated to Sept. 8, so the earliest he can return is Sept. 23; prospect Josue De Paula was called up from Double-A Tulsa.

briefs.headline: Shelton beats Tiafoe in four sets to reach his first Slam final
briefs.summary: Ben Shelton won 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 against Frances Tiafoe on Friday night at Arthur Ashe with 20 aces, the first American man in the U.S. Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972; he meets No. 1 Alexander Zverev on Sunday.

briefs.headline: Falcons rule Tagovailoa out; Cooper Rush starts Sunday at Pittsburgh
briefs.summary: Tua Tagovailoa strained an oblique in Thursday's practice and was ruled out Friday for the 1 p.m. ET opener at the Steelers; Cooper Rush, 32, with 16 career starts, replaces him with Michael Penix Jr. already out.

briefs.headline: Kawhi Leonard's trade to Toronto stays on hold as Clippers reorganize
briefs.summary: The June 30 deal cannot close until the Clippers name a basketball operations chief and an acting governor the NBA approves after owner Steve Ballmer's suspension; Leonard paid a $700,000 fine and federal prosecutors are investigating.

briefs.headline: No. 23 Missouri wins the Border War 38-21 at Kansas
briefs.summary: Austin Simmons threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns and Jamal Roberts ran for 125 Friday night in Lawrence, where Missouri outgained Kansas 469-255 and forced three turnovers; the Tigers are 2-0.

sections.label: In Season

coming_in.item: Opens today. The general squirrel season runs from this morning through Feb. 28, and the summary table sets the daily bag at six and the possession limit at 24, with no season limit and no registration requirement.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

coming_in.item: Seven days out. The migratory bird summary, downloaded and read in full this morning, lists Saturday, Sept. 19, and Oct. 31 as the two single youth waterfowl days for ducks, geese, coots, gallinules and mergansers; its footnote (b), legible today where it was not Friday, says the youth-day bag is the same as the daily limit of the regular duck and goose seasons, except that two scaup may be taken as part of the six-duck daily bag. Hunters under 15 must be accompanied by a licensed adult 18 or older who may not hunt, and every licensed hunter needs a HIP registration card.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

coming_in.item: Seven days out. The second gun window for bear runs Sept. 19-25 in SELECTED COUNTIES, a list the summary table does not carry, so no county is named here; the county-by-county limits are on pamphlet pages 33-39 and vary by permit class. Electronic registration is required.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

coming_in.item: Two weeks out. Archery and crossbow seasons for deer and for bear both open Saturday, Sept. 26, and run through Dec. 31, with electronic registration required for each; the deer and bear bag limits are not in the summary table at all, only on pamphlet pages 13-18 and 33-39, and are not printed here.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

prime.item: This weekend. The youth, Class Q and Class XS bear season is today and Sunday, Sept. 12-13, with a second two-day window Oct. 17-18; the summary table refers readers to pamphlet page 34 for the limits rather than printing them, and electronic registration is required.
prime.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

prime.item: The first dove segment is in its second week and runs through Oct. 11, with a daily bag of 15 and a possession limit of 45, per the migratory bird summary read this morning; shooting hours after opening day are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset, and HIP registration is required.
prime.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

prime.item: The Marine Fisheries limits page, effective Sept. 2 and opened this morning, holds red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one a day, with the harvest reported to the division. In the Fisherman's Post September report, published Sept. 1 and 11 days old, Native Son called the dock and creek-mouth bite steady on topwater early and natural bait once the sun is up, and Spring Tide had over-slot schools of 28 to 32 inches that are gone the next day from wherever they were left.

Limits page: 14 to 20 inches total length, three a day, one of the three allowed over 26 inches. East Coast Sports' paragraph in the Sept. 1 report has some trout coming on live and artificial baits around structure and grass banks, early or late to avoid the midday heat, and Surf City Pier has them in the early morning and evening; an 11-day-old monthly report, not this morning's water.

Limits page: 12-inch fork length, 15 a day. East Coast Sports has surf and pier anglers catching Spanish on casting jigs with the early-morning bite best, Native Son is seeing a better class of fish over 3 pounds off the beach alongside high numbers of smaller ones, and Surf City Pier has them on Gotcha plugs, all in the Sept. 1 report.

The limits page's bluefish row carries no minimum size and a footnote, opened this morning, that sets the creel at three fish per person per day in all private recreational fishing and five per person per day aboard a for-hire vessel. Jolly Roger Pier's Sept. 1 paragraph called bluefish and Spanish hit-or-miss on plugs at surface-feeding schools, early and late.

Limits page: 14-inch minimum, 25-inch maximum total length, 10 a day. Surf City Pier's bottom fishing in the Sept. 1 report produced black drum, pompano and croakers, and Jolly Roger's bottom rigs had black drum in the mix with red drum, Virginia mullet and specks.

Limits page: 14 inches total length, five a day. No Topsail shop mentions them in the Sept. 1 report; the reference calendar's pattern, fiddler crabs tight to pilings and oyster bars on moving water, is the only guide and is not a live report.

going_out.item: Closes tomorrow. The migratory bird summary's table, read from the PDF this morning, ends the early Canada goose season Sunday, Sept. 13; the regular Canada and white-fronted goose season then opens its first split Oct. 3-18, with Nov. 7-15 and Dec. 8 - Jan. 31 to follow, at five a day and 15 in possession in aggregate. The early-season bag limit did not come through legibly in this morning's extraction of the table and is not printed.
going_out.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

going_out.item: Day 12 of 14, two days left. Proclamation FF-27-2026, opened again this morning as the PDF behind the limits page's link, makes it unlawful to possess flounder for recreational purposes after 11:59 p.m. Monday, Sept. 14; through then it is one fish per person per day at a 15-inch minimum total length, one daily limit per person aboard a vessel, no harvest under a Recreational Commercial Gear License, and the harvest must be reported. The limits table shows Sept. 15-30 closed. Carolina Flats' Sept. 1 report had a 20-to-24-inch class on live mullet or a 1-ounce bucktail with a Gulp trailer.

sections.note: Gauley season is in its second day. The National Park Service's Gauley River whitewater page, last updated Aug. 26 and opened this morning, lists Summersville Lake releases Sept. 11-14, 18-21 and 25-28 and Oct. 2-5, 9-12 and 17-18; the park's Aug. 24 Letter to Gauley Boaters, also opened this morning, gives the season as Sept. 11 - Oct. 17 and closes the Tailwaters Campground Sept. 11-28 for parking work. The Monongahela alerts page, opened this morning, still carries the Forest Road 19 Dolly Sods closure beginning Sept. 14 under order 09-21-01-26-07, the Sept. 8 Forest Road 76 Cranberry River closure under order 09-21-02-26-05, and the Aug. 12 Tea Creek Campground and Forest Road 86 construction alert with work under way since Aug. 28; fire danger is posted low and nothing new is dated Sept. 9-12. The WVDNR migratory bird PDF downloaded with certificate verification this morning and its season table and footnotes were read in full. The Marine Fisheries proclamation index opened on two addresses but its first page tops out at FF-24-2026 of April 16 and does not show FF-27 itself, so it cannot be read as complete; nothing newer than FF-27 was found, which is not the same as nothing issued. A search for September trout stocking returned only the DNR's January return-of-stocking release and its stocking-schedule page, which sits on the wvdnr.gov site this desk cannot open; no September stocking notice was found and none is printed. The WV hunting reference file is valid through June 30, 2027.

waters.working: Up from 44.2 cfs at this hour Friday, and the stage is nine hundredths higher at 1.34 feet: Friday's showers put a small bump in the river overnight, the first upward move in a week of falling water. It is still low, still wadeable everywhere, and a bump this size on a freestone stream is a good thing, a little color off the banks and a reason for fish that had been pinned in the plunge pools to slide back into the pocket water between them. That makes this morning less of a stalking problem than Friday was: a 9-foot leader to 5X will do instead of the 12-footer, a size 14 or 16 caddis pupa or a soft-hackle swung through the pockets on the first of the rise, a size 14 black stonefly nymph dead-drifted down the seams into each pool, and an olive sculpin streamer bumped along the undercut banks while the light is low and the water carries any tint. Caddis, stoneflies and sculpin are the forage. The window is the morning. NWS Charleston's forecast for Cowen, generated 5:39 a.m., has showers and storms likely from 1 p.m. on with a 60% chance, then 70% tonight with a quarter to half an inch, and a flood watch is in effect for Webster County from noon today until 1 a.m. Sunday; the 5:29 a.m. discussion has precipitable water near 2 inches and light steering flow, a renewed flash-flood threat, and the watch widened a tier of counties eastward on the terrain. A half inch on ground that took Friday's rain moves a freestone river fast; be off the water when the storms arrive.
waters.note: A Flood Watch issued at 1:58 a.m. by NWS Charleston runs for Webster County from noon today until 1 a.m. Sunday. The Monongahela alerts page has nothing new for the Williams: the Aug. 12 Tea Creek Campground and Forest Road 86 construction alert stands, the Sept. 8 Forest Road 76 order is on the Cranberry side, and the Forest Road 19 order is for Dolly Sods from Sept. 14.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 24.7 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Down 0.99 feet from 25.68 at this hour Friday: the Kanawha and Mason County creek water from Thursday's rain has passed through the pool and the gauge is back near where it sat Thursday. That is a clearing river at normal pool, and a clearing river fishes structure, not slack. Shad are the forage, so the first stop is the current side of the wing-dam tips and the riprap on the outside bends with a white or shad-pattern swimbait on a half-ounce head and a shad-colored square-bill crankbait knocked along the rock; keep the chartreuse-and-white spinnerbait for the creek mouths, where the last of the color hangs, and a black-and-blue jig for the barge-cut edges. Fish it early. NWS Charleston's forecast for Point Pleasant, generated 5:39 a.m., has fog until 10 a.m., showers and storms likely by late afternoon with a 60% chance and a tenth to a quarter inch, then 90% tonight with a quarter to half an inch, and a flood watch runs for Mason County from noon until 1 a.m. Sunday; the 5:29 a.m. discussion puts the greatest flash-flood risk in the Mid-Ohio Valley, where soils are wet from this week's rain and the high-resolution ensembles give better than a 50% chance of more than 3 inches in spots. The creeks will color the pool again tonight if that verifies.
waters.note: This is the pool side, 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam; USGS does not gauge the Byrd tailwater, and no Corps lock notice is printed. The Weather Service has no river forecast point at Point Pleasant; Huntington is the forecast gauge. A Flood Watch is in effect for Mason County from noon today until 1 a.m. Sunday.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 26.6 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Down 1.95 feet from 28.54 at this hour Friday. The crest came and went: the fetcher's trend flag reads rising against its own 24-hour comparison, but the NWPS observed trace, read at 5:40 a.m., has the gauge between 26.59 and 26.79 feet from 1:15 to 5 a.m., which is a river holding flat at normal pool, not one climbing. NWS Huntington's forecast, issued 11:09 a.m. Friday, had 26.3 feet through today, a nudge back up to 26.8 by 8 p.m. Sunday, then a slow slide to 25.5 by Wednesday morning, no flooding; the observed water is running about three-tenths above that line. Shad, skipjack and crawfish are the forage, and with the current off the lock wall and the wing dams the structure fishes again: a white or skipjack-pattern swimbait across the faces of the wing-dam tips and along the lock wall at first light for the bass and hybrids that were pinned in the eddies Friday, a three-quarter-ounce crawfish-colored football jig dragged down the riprap, and the barge-cut mouths on the way back. The forecast for Huntington, generated 5:39 a.m., has fog before 9 a.m., storms possible from 9 a.m. and likely by late afternoon with a 60% chance, then 80% tonight, a tenth to a quarter inch each period; a flood watch covers Cabell County from noon until 1 a.m. Sunday, and the discussion's heaviest rain sits up the valley in the Parkersburg direction, so the next rise, if any, arrives from upstream after the weekend.
waters.note: This is the gauge below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, not the tailwater. The Corps' Huntington District site was not tried this morning and no lock notice is printed. The NWS forecast predates today's rain and may be reissued; the observed trace is from the NWPS API at 5:40 a.m.

waters.reading: Sound lows 3:52 AM at 0.3 ft and 4:14 PM at 0.5 ft at Hampstead; highs 9:40 AM at 4.2 ft and 10:01 PM at 4.0 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 9:40 AM and 10:01 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The Fisherman's Post September report is 11 days old, published Tuesday, Sept. 1, and the feed opened this morning carries nothing newer, so it is the month's pattern and not this morning's water. Different voices from it today: East Coast Sports has reds and some trout on live and artificial baits around structure and grass banks, early or late, Spanish and bluefish on casting jigs from the surf and piers in the first hours of light, a few tarpon and cobia on live baits off the pier ends, and flounder everywhere; Native Son has the red drum steady at docks and creek mouths, topwater plugs at first light and then deeper, slower or on natural bait once the sun is up, with flounder in the deeper holes against structure and grass banks; Carolina Flats has the mullet thick inshore and 20-to-24-inch flounder on a live mullet or a 1-ounce bucktail with a Gulp curly tail. Set against today's sound tides, first light lands in the middle of the flood from the 3:52 a.m. low to the 9:40 a.m. high, which is the secondary drum window, fish pushing up into the flooded grass and the dock flats, and the topwater hour; the fall from 9:40 to the 4:14 p.m. low is the main red drum window at the creek mouths and oyster bars, with the last two hours, roughly 2 to 4 p.m., the part that matters, cut menhaden or a finger mullet a couple of feet off the channel edge; flounder on the first of the push after 4:14 against dock pilings and the ICWW channel edges; trout after dark on the rising water toward the 10:01 p.m. high, under the dock lights with a shrimp imitation. The moon was new at 11:27 p.m. ET Thursday, per the U.S. Naval Observatory, and the fetcher's phase is new moon at 0% illumination: spring tides, a 3.9-foot swing in the sound this morning and 3.5 feet this evening, the hardest current of the month through the inlet and the most bait moving. Flounder harvest has two days left, through Monday. Water 83.3F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast.
waters.note: NWS Wilmington's 5:35 a.m. surf zone forecast for Coastal Pender, including Surf City and Topsail Beach, has a LOW rip current risk today and Sunday, surf 1 to 3 feet, a moderate thunderstorm potential and a moderate waterspout risk both days, a high UV index, water in the lower 80s, a chance of showers and storms, highs in the mid 80s, southwest winds 5 to 10 mph and a moderate south-to-north longshore current; Sunday's heat index reaches 100, and the extended turns the rip risk moderate Tuesday and Wednesday on northeast winds around 15 mph with surf to 4 feet. No alert was in effect for Pender County at 5:40 a.m. The National Hurricane Center's 2 a.m. Atlantic outlook expects no tropical cyclone formation in the next seven days. Hampstead is the sound station and the tide that matters; the surf forecast's inlet times, high 8:48 a.m. and low 2:57 p.m., run 52 and 77 minutes ahead of the sound today.

kicker: The Aki basho opens tomorrow in Tokyo, one day out, with Onosato the lone yokozuna; the Rays and Brewers clinched Friday, Chelsea and Liverpool kick off at 10 a.m. ET, Spurs at 12:30 and WVU at 1.
